It’s not always about one specific thing—just this vague sense that something could go wrong. This has been going on for a few months, maybe longer, and it seems more noticeable recently. I’m still managing to work and take care of myself, but it feels like I’m always bracing for something without knowing exactly what.

These “what if” chains just take over, and I lose track of what I’m doing. I’ll reread the same report line three or four times because my mind keeps jumping to some future disaster. It’s been like this pretty much every day for at least the last year, maybe longer.

Physically, I feel like I’m wound up tight all the time, like a spring that never relaxes. I can’t sit still at my workbench; I’m fidgeting, pacing, checking things over and over—not because of a ritual, just because I feel so on edge. I catch myself clenching my teeth, especially when I’m stressing about upcoming appraisals, and my jaw aches and I get these dull headaches by the end of the day.

I feel wired, like I’m coiled too tight inside, almost vibrating in my chair. I can’t sit still; I’ll pace around the lab or tap my foot constantly.
